clue.text: Doubt American picture will be in Jerusalem

indicators.note: the picture is said to be placed in the name for Jerusalem, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is the hill of Jerusalem and a poetic name for the city
a pic is an informal word for a picture or photo

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether an American's photograph will end up on show in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Sion, also spelt Zion, is a biblical name for Jerusalem; 'will be in' places the picture after its first letter, giving SPICION.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of mistrust, a synonym of doubt as a noun.

clue.text: Vehicle in science fiction which can keep you warm in winter

definitions.text: which can keep you warm in winter

indicators.note: the vehicle is placed in the abbreviation, splitting its two letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A spacecraft from a sci-fi story that would heat its passengers in the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen neck wrap is worn for warmth in cold weather.

clue.text: Yon visits could lead to a complaint

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be reworked to produce something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Visiting that place yonder might make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could lead to' signals that YON and VISITS are rearranged into the nine-letter medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Synovitis is an inflammation of a joint's lining membrane, an ailment, which is what complaint means in medical usage.

clue.text: Showing lack of concern by flouting cautions?

indicators.note: flouting rules means disregarding their order, so these letters are thrown out of place

parts.note: the fodder word, which as printed lacks two of the needed letters

explanation.surface: Someone shows they do not care by ignoring warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flouting' rearranges CAUTIONS, but that gives only eight of the ten letters: the clue gives no source for IN, so the setter probably meant 'in flouting cautions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciant means carefree and nonchalant, showing indifference.

clue.text: This is hard male, outcast

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: read as cast out, the letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a tough man rejected by society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcast' rearranges MALE as MAEL. The whole clue is also the definition: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was driven out into the desert in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Ishmael was banished with his mother, so his name has come to mean a social exile.

clue.text: Female name that is associated with South African province

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa (now KwaZulu-Natal)
ie is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A girl's name said to have links with a region of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a common given name for girls.

clue.text: In park I roved to find Russian ballet

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone wandering through a park comes across a Russian dance company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kirov is the famous St Petersburg ballet company, now called the Mariinsky.

clue.text: Considerate daughter goes with relatives

parts.note: kin means one's relatives
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A thoughtful girl goes off with her family.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and considerate are both synonyms for thoughtful towards others.

clue.text: Repeat regarding cricket score

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: Something to do with a score in a game of cricket being repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme.

clue.text: Country providing venue -laze about

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a jumbled state, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A nation offers a place where visitors can lounge around.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela is a nation in South America.

clue.text: Times includes name-woman's name

indicators.note: the word for times is said to contain the abbreviation, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: ages means long periods of time

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper prints a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a traditional girl's name.

clue.text: Success and what it does? Not altogether an accident

parts.note: a hit is a success, as a show or song
taken as written
a successful show has a long run, so running is what a hit does

explanation.surface: A question about what success brings, with a hint at a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because in this kind of crash the driver leaves deliberately: the collision may be accidental, the fleeing is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A road incident where the driver flees the scene is only partly accidental, since leaving is a choice.

clue.text: Story about Bible for us is advantageous

indicators.note: the story is put about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: a fable is a story
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
something for us is ours, so our

explanation.surface: A story about the Bible is said to be good for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AVOUR inside FABLE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Favourable means helpful or beneficial, as advantageous does.

clue.text: Spanish woman, one backing religion

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Spanish lady who supports a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the religion into NEZ. Inez is the Spanish form of Agnes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inez is a Spanish girl's name, a form of Agnes.

clue.text: Telling off artist interrupting his exhibition around university

indicators.note: the show is wrapped around the university abbreviation
the artist breaks into the word for the show, so goes inside it

parts.note: a hanging is an exhibition of pictures on gallery walls
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter rudely interrupts his own show at a university, scolding people.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician; 'interrupting' gives HARANGING, and 'around' then wraps that round the university letter. 'his' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Haranguing is lecturing someone at length, a form of scolding.

clue.text: Soak and liar prepared for another court appearance

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

indicators.note: a thing prepared has been made ready or put into shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A drunkard and a liar get ready for a second trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' tempts as the noun for a drunkard; here it is the verb RET. 'prepared' rearranges LIAR as RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a second hearing of a case in court.

clue.text: Telescope is endlessly difficult to deal with

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: refractory means stubborn and hard to manage

explanation.surface: A telescope proves forever awkward to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A refractor is a telescope that uses lenses rather than mirrors.

clue.text: An illustration from old flame — enough

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means plenty or enough

explanation.surface: A picture drawn by a former lover is quite sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is an instance used to illustrate a point.

clue.text: Copy snap figure

parts.note: a snap is a photograph
a stat is a statistic, a figure

explanation.surface: Instruction to copy a figure from a snapshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Photostat is a photocopy, from an early trade name for the process.

clue.text: Fabric, first instance thereof, is hard to get

parts.note: the first letter of the fabric word, its first instance
to net is to get or gain

explanation.surface: The first example of a cloth is hard to obtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thereof' refers back to 'Fabric', so its first letter, F, starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is an open mesh fabric used for tights and stockings.

clue.text: Still about to eat bread? Mad to be off it!

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the bread inside it, as if eating it
about means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
a roll is a piece of bread

explanation.surface: Someone is still about to eat bread, and is told they must be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the word for still into TEY. 'Off one's trolley' is British slang for mad, so the definition is the thing a mad person is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off one's trolley is an idiom meaning crazy, so this cart is the thing a mad person is off.

clue.text: Duncan, perhaps, is one mending road?

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: something being mended is reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man named Duncan is a road repairer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duncan' looks like a surname or a man; it is Isadora Duncan, the American dancer. 'mending' rearranges ROAD as DORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan was a pioneer of modern dance, an example of someone with that forename.

clue.text: The writer to demand one addressed? Really!

parts.note: the writer is the setter speaking of themself, I
to ask is to demand
the person spoken to is you

explanation.surface: The author makes a demand of a person spoken to, in exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of exasperation, like 'honestly!'

clue.text: Water seen in sea quaking

indicators.note: seen in says the answer can be spotted inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Water visible in a sea that is shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is Latin for water, used in English in compounds and labels.

clue.text: Taking cap off had drink lifted

indicators.note: a cap is a top, so taking it off removes the first letter

parts.note: supped means drank

explanation.surface: Someone removed their hat, had a drink and raised it.
explanation.definitionFit: Upped means raised or increased, as lifted does.

clue.text: Morning's so organised for church dignitaries

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters of mornings

explanation.surface: Morning is so well arranged for senior clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignor is a title of honour for senior Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Second inferior track

parts.note: poor means inferior in quality

explanation.surface: Another poor-quality path.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of an animal, its track.

clue.text: Some exotic editors needed to be cooled down

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some exotic editors needed calming down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'needed to be cooled down' as the definition, but that cannot stand for the answer; 'needed to be' is a link and 'cooled down' alone means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means chilled, made cold.

clue.text: Mostly to choose friend in a relevant way?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to pick means to choose
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Choosing a friend in a suitable manner, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of TO PICK, giving TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Topically means in a way connected to current matters, pertinent.

clue.text: Involved with securing right beginning to song

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the first word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: into means keen on or involved with

explanation.surface: A musician keen on getting things right at the start of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Woman in scarlet worked again

indicators.note: the woman is placed in the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A woman in a red dress has done it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid means did again, did over.

clue.text: Lad needing rest disturbed by Mormon leader

parts.note: Brigham Young led the Mormon church after Joseph Smith

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy wants sleep but a Mormon elder keeps waking him.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, such as a boy.
